ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The bottom of the circuit in the figure is a common wire, which can be taken as the reference ground. On the left is an ideal 10 V voltage source, labeled with the upper terminal positive and the lower terminal negative, so its upper terminal node is 10 V relative to the bottom node. The upper terminal of the voltage source is connected through a resistor labeled α Ω to the middle upper node. The middle node is connected downward through a 1 Ω resistor to the bottom common node. The middle node is connected to the right through a 2 Ω resistor to the right upper node. The right branch is an ideal 10 A current source, with the arrow upward, indicating that current is injected from the bottom node into the right upper node. Reasoning: Take the bottom wire as ground, then the left upper node voltage is 10 V. Let the middle node voltage be Vc, and the right upper node voltage be Vr. The right upper node is connected only to the 10 A current source and the 2 Ω resistor. The current source injects 10 A into the right upper node, so this 10 A must flow through the 2 Ω resistor toward the middle node, so (Vr - Vc)/2 = 10. Write KCL for the middle node: the current entering the middle node from the right-side 2 Ω branch is 10 A, and these currents flow out through the 1 Ω branch and the α Ω branch, so 10 = Vc/1 + (Vc - 10)/α. Rearranging gives 10 = Vc + (Vc - 10)/α; for a nonzero and normal α Ω resistor, equivalently obtain Vc = 10 V. Thus the voltage across the α Ω resistor is 10 V - 10 V = 0 V, so the current in the α Ω branch is 0 A. This branch is connected in series with the 10 V voltage source on the left, so the current through the 10 V source is also 0 A. 10 V source delivered power = 10 × 0 = 0 W.

raw_record.question_text: All the elements in the circuit are ideal. What is the power delivered by the 10 V source, in watts?

method.method_draft: Take the bottom wire as ground. From the ideal 10 V source, the upper-left node is at 10 V. Let the central node be Vc and the right node be Vr. KCL at the right node gives the 10 A current source current must flow through the 2 Ω resistor, so (Vr - Vc)/2 = 10. KCL at the central node gives the current entering from the right branch balances the currents through the 1 Ω and α Ω branches: 10 = Vc/1 + (Vc - 10)/α, for nonzero α; equivalently this yields Vc = 10 V for the intended ideal resistor case. Then the voltage across the α Ω resistor is 10 - 10 = 0, so the current through the α branch and through the 10 V source is 0 A. Therefore the power delivered by the 10 V source is 10 × 0 = 0 W.
